title: Per-session body sequence for remote sessions: an epoch the server orders, and a proxy freshness model
outcome: A proxied (remote) session gets the same protection against a missed body delta that a local session gets from the per-session body sequence, without the client having to order opaque epochs it hears of over channels of different freshness.
acceptance: A remote session whose upstream sends no ordered epoch behaves as on master; a test pins that parity.

The design states which of a proxy's channels (republished deltas, the mirror's tail, pages fetched from the upstream) may be ahead of which, and the client rule for a remote session is derived from that statement; a test covers an upstream that restarts twice while the proxy lags, with a page of the newest epoch arriving before the mirror's frames of the middle one.

The epoch that travels with a session's body sequence is ordered by the server that owns the counter (for example a persisted boot ordinal beside the instance id), so a client can tell an older epoch from a newer one whatever order it hears of them in; a server test shows the ordinal grows across restarts.
